en.summary: This maxim, often cited in the context of the Battle of Siffin, establishes the jurisprudential principle of 'defensive jihad' by distinguishing between the initiator (bagh) and the responder. It underscores the Shia emphasis on restraint and legitimacy in warfare, where the burden of proof for aggression lies with the one who calls for single combat. The phrase 'the aggressor is slain' (al-baghiya masru'un) links this specific etiquette to the broader Quranic concept of divine retribution against those who transgress boundaries.

Frasa 'yang agresor dibunuh' (al-baghiya masru'un) menghubungkan etika spesifik ini dengan konsep Al-Qur'an yang lebih luas tentang pembalasan ilahi terhadap mereka yang melampaui batas.
